ai.description: The Shiradi Night Frog is a small, brown amphibian with a snout-vent length of 25–30 mm. It features a distinct, pointed snout and granular skin with prominent, irregular dorsal folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus shiradi* is best distinguished by its unique, significantly elongated third finger, which is distinctly longer than the others compared to similar species.
ai.habitat: The Shiradi Night Frog inhabits evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky streams at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Shiradi Night Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active near forest streams where males call from rocks or vegetation to attract mates during the monsoon season.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus shiradi* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying terrestrial clutches of 15–30 eggs on rocks or leaves near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Shiradi Night Frog is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Shiradi Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard calling from moss-covered rocks along fast-flowing forest streams.
